description.narrative:
Goal: To support women and Girls in Armenia in driving the gender equality agenda forward in post-revolutionary and post-crisis situation for a more inclusive, equal, and democratic society
The overall goal will be achieved through three objectives:
Objective 1: Women CSOs create safe and empowering spaces for women and girls to heal, learn, and engage in democratic processes.
Objective 2: Develop and utilize an intersectional movement and gender equality agenda to engage with stakeholders.
Objective 3: Strengthen organizational capacities of Womens CSOs to address gender stereotypes, inequalities, GBV and WPS issues

WRC har lämnat in förslaget "Support for Resilient Women's Civil Society Organizing in the Context of Multiple Crises in Armenia" till Sida för programstöd. Den föreslagna projektperioden är 36 månader med en föreslagen budget på 1 200 000 Euro, vilket uppskattas till cirka 12 000 000 SEK. Programmets förväntade resultat är: - Att stärka kvinnor i riktade områden/samhällen som drabbats av konflikten för att påverka beslutsfattande på lokal nivå. - Att öka civilsamhällets förmåga att bidra till en gendersensitiv Covid-19 återhämtning. - Att stärka den inter-sektionella medborgarrörelsen (civila samhället och aktivister) för att driva fram en effektiv policyrespons mot könsbaserat våld och agendan för kvinnor fred- och säkerhet.

WRC has submitted "Support for Resilient Women's Civil Society Organizing in the Context of Multiple Crises in Armenia" proposal to Sida for the programme support. The proposed duration of the project is 36 months with requested budget of 1 200 000 Euro, which is estimated to about 12 000 000 SEK. The outcomes of the programme are: - To empower women in the local communities affected by the conflict to influence at the local development. - To increase the capacities of CSOs to advocate for gender sensitive COVID-19 recovery. - To strengthen intersectional civic movement (CSOs and activists) to drive an effective policy response to Gender based Violence and Women Peace and Security Agendas.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The feminist activist space is strengthened including a wide range of educational and personal development programs to enhance the skills and knowledge among participants engaged in gender equality advocacy. The space is open to the community, and all interested in gender equality issues and women's rights to get informed and mobilize around their selected issues. The space is active and mobilized many groups around the issue of refugees, the fate of the forcibly displaced women and girls. Amid the crisis situations in Armenia, WRC had to adapt its activities to provide urgent humanitarian support, a shift happened, and WRC and its partners had to adapt fast and extended their services and counseling help to the forcibly displaced population.
Women's Resource Center advocacy team maintained its focus on advocating for legislation against workplace sexual harassment. Their efforts concluded with the release of the study titled "The Issue of Sexual Harassment in the Workplace in Armenia".
WRC being a member of three coalitions and contributed to the joint advocacy through the Coalition to Stop Violence against Women, the Non-discrimination and Equality Coalition, and the Human Rights House Yerevan. Joint advocacy within these coalitions was focused on combating gender-based violence, advocating for comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation, adoption of the National Gender Equity Strategy 2025-2028, and the third National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security 20252028.
n April 2024, the Armenian Parliament adopted WRC-supported amendments to the Domestic Violence Law, marking a key step in protecting individuals vulnerable to domestic violence. Key changes included expanded definitions that now covered intimate partners, extended durations for emergency and protection orders, and streamlined procedures for victim protection. Additionally, the amendments added an article criminalizing stalking to the Penal Code. These changes, effective July 1, 2024, enhanced protections and broaden support for domestic violence survivors. The major achievement has been the adoption by the Armenian Parliament of the regulations on self-managed regulations on medical abortions. As part of joint advocacy with the Non-Discrimination and Equality Coalition, WRC proposed amendments to the Draft Law on Equality emphasizing the need for a separate Equality Body, explicit inclusion of sexual orientation and gender identity as grounds for discrimination, and stronger accountability for violators.
Women's security issues and the WPS agenda remained priority topic for WRC. WRC organized consultations with civil society representatives to address the security challenges women face, with a particular emphasis on human security. These meetings aimed to identify and map the key issues affecting women, including forcibly displaced women from Nagorno-Karabakh, in crisis situations. A key concern raised was the absence of state response procedures during crises, including natural disasters.
